problem: Weather forecasting and climate modeling require unified approaches that work across diverse atmospheric tasks without task-specific customization.
approach: WIND is a foundation model pre-trained with self-supervised video reconstruction using unconditional diffusion, then solves diverse atmospheric problems as inverse problems via posterior sampling.
contribution: Demonstrates a single pre-trained model can replace specialized baselines across forecasting, downscaling, field reconstruction, and extreme weather exploration without fine-tuning.

problem: Reinforcement learning for LLM reasoning faces a bottleneck where high-quality training samples are scarce because exploration is limited by the model's inherent capabilities.
approach: RuscaRL uses checklist-style rubrics as external scaffolding during rollout generation to guide diverse high-quality responses, then gradually decays this guidance while using the same rubrics for verifiable reward scoring.
contribution: Breaks the exploration-learning cycle and improves reasoning across multiple benchmarks with more reliable reward signals for open-ended tasks.

problem: Large reasoning models produce complex reasoning traces with implicit structures, but existing evaluation methods lack unified principles for assessing quality and using evaluation signals for optimization.
approach: Characterize reasoning quality via macro/micro efficiency-effectiveness (ME² principle), model traces as directed acyclic graphs (DAGs), and train a Thinking Reward Model (TRM) on a DAG-based pairwise evaluation framework.
contribution: Thinking rewards provide effective optimization signals, achieving up to 19.3% gain at test time via better reasoning selection and up to 3.9% gain during RL training.

problem: Battery lifetime early prediction is hindered by extremely weak degradation signals buried in stochastic noise during initial cycles.
approach: DITING uses optimal-transport-based template matching and a tri-coupled degradation manifestation mechanism to exploit noise randomness: symmetric coupling suppresses noise while cumulative degradation propagates as bilateral discrepancies, mimicking the binaural effect.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance in detecting weak early-stage cues and provides reliable early support for full-lifecycle battery management.

problem: Data-free model merging for cross-domain tasks often fails because simple parameter heuristics ignore inter-layer dependencies and non-uniform expertise distribution.
approach: SA-Merging applies saliency scoring from structural pruning to task vectors, introduces merge-aware modulation to reduce interference, and iteratively removes non-informative updates while preserving connectivity.
contribution: Reduces the gap between data-free and test-time adaptation methods, with rank-wise decomposition supporting LoRA merging without compromising structure.

problem: Training multi-agent LLM systems for collaboration creates a moving-target problem: updating one agent shifts the context distribution for others, causing coordination regression.
approach: TeamTR uses a trust-region framework that evaluates updates on intermediate team states, enforces per-agent trust regions via token-decomposed reverse KL, and computes trust-region certificates from logged data.
contribution: Provides population-level per-update improvement guarantees, mitigates coordination regressions, and enables stable training of heterogeneous teams with modular component replacement.

problem: Current antibody language models treat all residues equally and inherit germline bias that down-weights functionally critical non-germline mutations as noise.
approach: PRISM explicitly represents germline and non-germline residues as distinct token types in a factorized 53-token vocabulary, enabling separate modeling of scaffold and binding-critical mutations.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art pseudo-perplexity on hypervariable regions, uniquely correlates with binding affinity across three deep mutational scanning landscapes, and enables controllable generation by decoupling scaffold and binding optimization.

problem: Convergent cross mapping for causal discovery suffers from weak manifold reconstruction when using time-delay embedding, leading to unreliable neighborhoods and poor causal identification under noise.
approach: TopoDistill aligns local neighborhood structure of delay embeddings to a multivariate global embedding via knowledge distillation, preserving smooth and reliable neighborhoods for cross mapping.
contribution: Improves causal discovery in multivariate time series by maintaining specificity against spurious correlations while enabling effective identification under noise.

problem: Multimodal models fail to generalize across domains because joint optimization causes encoders to exploit cross-modal co-occurrences (fusion overfitting) rather than learn domain-invariant features.
approach: MER-DG maximizes entropy of each encoder's feature distribution to preserve diversity, integrated as an additive loss term independent of architecture.
contribution: Improves average performance by ~5% over standard fusion and ~2% over state-of-the-art on EPIC-Kitchens and HAC benchmarks.

problem: The robustness mechanisms of LLMs against character-level perturbations (typos, shuffling, invisible characters) remain unclear.
approach: Investigates three types of character-level perturbations and explores how LLMs implicitly handle chaotic segmentation and fragmented tokenization through both implicit and explicit perturbation removal mechanisms.
contribution: Reveals that LLMs maintain notable performance even under severe perturbations, unveiling architectural strengths and potential misuse risks.

problem: Differentially private training requires higher signal-to-noise ratio but existing analyses overlook the distinction between label-dependent feature signals and label-independent noise.
approach: Provides first theoretical framework analyzing private training via feature learning on multi-patch data, characterizing signal learning and noise memorization separately in noisy gradient descent.
contribution: Shows private signal learning requires higher SNR than non-private, and proves that noise memorization in non-private learning transfers to private learning, reducing generalization.

problem: Multimodal geometry reasoning requires joint understanding of visual diagrams and structured symbolic inference, but models lack sufficient training data and weak visual-symbolic alignment.
approach: Synthesizes complex geometry problems via symbolic seed construction, grounded instantiation with verification, and code-based rendering; uses code prediction as explicit alignment objective.
contribution: GeoCode demonstrates higher structural complexity than existing benchmarks while maintaining mathematical correctness, showing consistent improvements on multiple geometry benchmarks.

problem: Diffusion models for text struggle because Gaussian diffusion in continuous spaces loses token discreteness while categorical simplex approaches disregard semantic token relations.
approach: Smoothie progressively smooths token embeddings based on semantic similarity, combining continuous latent space strengths with discrete token handling and natural decoding.
contribution: Outperforms existing diffusion-based text models on sequence-to-sequence and unconditional generation, with better performance in both embedding space and categorical simplex baselines.

problem: Preference-based RL from trajectory comparisons suffers from training-inference mismatch: utilities trained on trajectory/segment level are applied per-step, causing distribution shift and poor temporal credit assignment.
approach: PAWS aligns utility training with policy optimization by performing policy updates directly using segment-level advantage functions derived from trajectory preferences.
contribution: Preserves trajectory-level preference information and avoids unreliable per-step signals, consistently outperforming existing preference-based RL methods on manipulation and locomotion.

problem: Classifier-free guidance relies on heuristic linear extrapolation that is sensitive to guidance scale, with limited principled understanding of its mechanisms.
approach: Interprets CFG through optimization: velocity field corresponds to gradients of smoothed distance functions, revealing CFG as approximation with prediction gap governing sensitivity; reformulates as homotopy optimization with manifold projection and Anderson Acceleration.
contribution: Training-free methods refine generation fidelity, prompt alignment, and robustness across DiT-XL-2-256, Flux, and Stable Diffusion 3.5 with significant improvements.

problem: Operations research practitioners debug infeasible models through iterative inspection and repair, but LLM benchmarks treat OR as one-shot problem-to-code translation, omitting the diagnostic loop.
approach: Formalizes infeasible-model repair as solver-in-the-loop MDP with deterministic IIS feedback, introduces ORLoopBench with 5,362 LP/MILP repair instances and operational decision benchmarks; applies RLVR training.
contribution: Solver-verified training enables 8B model to surpass frontier APIs on LP repair (95.3% vs 92.4%), improves diagnostic behavior, and reveals semantic drift in code regeneration.

problem: Generalized category discovery relies on contrastive learning with conflicting uniformity and consistency objectives, hindering formation of class-discriminative and semantically coherent structures.
approach: CURE uses two-stage framework: first learns category-anchored representations aligned with known prototypes, then extends via consistency with unified semantic regularization and Semantic Exploration Energy mechanism.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance and substantially reduces the gap between known and novel category performance.

problem: Variational inference in high-dimensional spaces requires scalable optimization methods for Gaussian probability measures.
approach: Proposes zeroth-order algorithm using interacting Gaussian particles in Linearized Bures-Wasserstein (LBW) space, a novel parametrization enabling efficient computation via consensus-based optimization.
contribution: Establishes well-posedness and convergence properties; demonstrates robustness and superior performance on variational inference tasks compared to gradient-based methods on non-log-concave targets.

problem: Single-cell gene expression generation is challenging due to count nature of data, complex latent dependencies, and lack of respect for exchangeability property.
approach: scLDM uses VAE with permutation-invariant pooling via Multi-head Cross-Attention Block (MCAB), replaces Gaussian prior with latent diffusion using Diffusion Transformers, enables multi-conditional generation.
contribution: Superior performance on observational and perturbational data with downstream cell classification, respecting data exchangeability.

problem: Standard PCA is highly sensitive to mean-shift contamination: small fractions of shifted samples cause large deviations in principal components.
approach: Uses random matrix theory to prove mean-shift spikes are spectrally separable and original eigenspace is asymptotically invariant; proposes two-stage algorithm adding knockoff mean-shift perturbation.
contribution: Removes mean-shift component using only standard PCA operations, exploiting spectral stability against contamination.

problem: Graph neural networks are vulnerable to unauthorized use, and existing watermarking relies on data manipulation which introduces ownership ambiguity and vulnerability to poisoning.
approach: Watermarks GNN explanations so they are statistically distinct from others; ownership verified through statistical significance without data manipulation.
contribution: Theoretically proves locating the watermark is NP-hard; demonstrates robustness to fine-tuning and pruning attacks while eliminating data dependencies.

problem: AI model hubs with thousands of pre-trained models require efficient scaling of model selection and continual updating as new models and tasks appear.
approach: Formalizes continual model routing (CMR) problem; proposes CARvE, a contrastive embedding approach using domain-stratified coreset replay and checkpoint-based anchoring for efficient routing.
contribution: CARvE significantly outperforms zero-shot retrieval, fine-tuning, and adapter-merging on model, family, and domain-level accuracy.

problem: Circuit discovery methods are brittle: identified circuits depend strongly on concept datasets and often fail to transfer out-of-distribution, raising questions about whether they capture true concepts.
approach: Wraps any circuit discovery algorithm with randomized data subsampling to certify that inclusion decisions are invariant to bounded edit-distance dataset perturbations.
contribution: Certified circuits achieve up to 56% higher accuracy and 80% fewer components while remaining reliable where baselines degrade, putting circuit discovery on formal ground.

problem: Existing LLM-based approaches struggle with deep protocol-level logic bugs involving complex state-dependent behaviors across multiple execution stages in consensus protocols.
approach: Agora uses domain-aware multi-agent framework with specialized agents that collaboratively explore protocol state spaces, synthesize attack scenarios, and validate findings iteratively.
contribution: Discovers 15 previously unknown protocol-level logic bugs violating safety properties, while existing LLM agents fail to detect any such bugs.

problem: Spectroscopic molecular structure elucidation is challenging due to spectral ambiguity, vast molecular space, and difficulty learning robust spectra-structure relationships from limited paired data.
approach: MAST introduces explicit motif priors as intermediate evidence throughout diffusion denoising and casts sampling as reward-guided tree search to prioritize high-reward trajectories.
contribution: Achieves 94.89% exact recovery on QM9S with improved 3D fidelity and high chemical validity while operating under limited computational budgets.

problem: Retrieval-augmented generation produces unsupported statements and unreliable citations despite strong retrievers, as sentences can remain factually unsupported.
approach: CiteGuard treats sentence-level factuality as multiple-testing problem, converts claim-evidence scores to p-values via conformal calibration, uses Benjamini-Hochberg procedures for false-discovery-rate control.
contribution: Reduces false-discovery rate among accepted claims from 28-31% to below 10% at α=0.10, retaining 86-92% of supported claims with finite-sample guarantees.

problem: Irregular time series modeling with continuous-discrete state-space models is computationally expensive or constrained by restrictive posterior assumptions.
approach: SDEVI performs variational inference directly on joint distribution of discrete-time observations while maintaining consistency with underlying SDE process; uses linear time-varying SDEs for scalable inference and extends to complex domain.
contribution: State-of-the-art performance on interpolation, extrapolation, regression, and classification across healthcare, physics, climate, and IoT benchmarks.

problem: Controllable generation with discrete diffusion models suffers from high computational overhead or requires retraining.
approach: GILC repurposes pretrained denoising network as variational proxy; introduces Jacobian-free mechanism for stable guidance by directly correcting clean prediction logits.
contribution: Plug-and-play guidance accommodating both differentiable and non-differentiable rewards, achieving state-of-the-art performance on DNA, protein, and molecular generation without additional training.

problem: Modeling complex dynamics leads to entanglement of static state representations and instantaneous motion, causing accumulated errors and off-manifold hallucinations that violate geometric constraints.
approach: Geometric Flow Grounding enforces evolution strictly along tangent bundle via differentiable Neural Tangent Projection Layer, geometrically decoupling state representation from tangential dynamics.
contribution: Reduces numerical aliasing in sparse systems, recovers interpretable gene regulatory motifs, provides zero-shot deepfake detection via projection residual inconsistencies.

problem: Coupled spatiotemporal forecasting suffers from reciprocal error amplification: errors from each subsystem propagate and amplify, causing rapid prediction collapse.
approach: PnP-Corrector decouples physical simulation from error correction by freezing pre-trained engines and training correction agent to proactively counteract systematic biases; uses DSLCast architecture.
contribution: On 300-day ocean-atmosphere forecast, reduces error 28% and surpasses state-of-the-art on key metrics.

problem: 3D Gaussian Splatting degrades in real-world environments due to transient distractors like moving objects and varying shadows, while existing methods rely on fragile semantic priors.
approach: 3DGS-HPC combines patch-wise classification for robust region-level decisions with hybrid classification integrating photometric and perceptual cues adaptively.
contribution: Improves robustness in mitigating distractors for 3DGS-based novel view synthesis.

problem: ADHD detection methods have received less attention to short-term brain functional reorganization, potentially missing important diagnostic signals.
approach: Proposes model using short-term windows for brain map sequence construction, short-term state and temporal dependency encoder, brain function memory to capture associations, combined with GNN-based long-term features.
contribution: Superior performance on ADHD-200 and OpenNeuro-ds002424 neuroimaging datasets for brain disorder detection.

problem: Electronic health records have distinct characteristics from natural language, but existing foundation models rely on suboptimal NLP-based approaches.
approach: Proposes pretraining with Pathology-Focused Binning for clinically significant quantization, Dual-Calendar RoPE for absolute/relative temporal signals, and Time-Conditioned Foreseeing objective aligning with clinical planning.
contribution: Outperforms existing foundation models on eleven downstream tasks (up to 54% AUPRC improvement), enables generation of realistic temporally consistent patient trajectories.

problem: Graph foundation models have fixed architectures mismatched to diverse downstream graph tasks, limiting generalization.
approach: AdaR uses recurrent graph model with adaptive test-time computing, encodes normalized step information and representation-target relations, employs gradient-based supervision for convergence.
contribution: Consistently outperforms baselines in both inductive and transductive settings without changing model parameters.

problem: Test-time scaling of diffusion models via computing expected future reward faces limitations: backward rollout is expensive while existing approaches suffer from bias and sampling issues.
approach: LiDAR computes expected future reward using only marginal samples from pretrained model, enabling closed-form guidance without backprop; uses lookahead sampling and efficient solver.
contribution: Achieves same GenEval performance as gradient guidance on SDXL with 9.5× speedup.

problem: Video generation models struggle with spatial consistency and object permanence in realistic simulation of physics-driven interactions.
approach: 3DGSim jointly trains inverse rendering and dynamics forecasting on multi-view RGB videos, uses MVSplat for particle representation, Point Transformer for dynamics, Gaussian Splatting for rendering.
contribution: Captures diverse behaviors from rigid to cloth dynamics while producing realistic lighting; generalizes to out-of-distribution cases despite training only on single-body collisions.

problem: End-to-end GPU program generation is challenging because existing methods focus on single-kernel optimization and do not address whole-system design, host-side settings, or practical deployment.
approach: StitchCUDA uses multi-agent framework (Planner/Coder/Verifier) with rubric-based agentic RL training Coder on task-to-code and feedback-driven optimization skills using real execution feedback.
contribution: Achieves nearly 100% success rate on end-to-end GPU tasks, 1.72× better speedup over multi-agent baseline and 2.73× over RL baseline.

problem: LLM moderation requires balancing performance and efficiency while supporting customization to user-specific requirements.
approach: MLPM leverages prototypes of intermediate representations across multiple layers for improved moderation quality, adding negligible overhead and supporting seamless application to any model.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on diverse moderation benchmarks with strong scalability across model families, integrates smoothly into end-to-end pipelines.

problem: Vision-language models suffer performance degradation on downstream tasks with noisy labels because filtering and reconstruction methods propagate errors.
approach: Evidence-Prompt treats prompt learning as Bayesian reasoning integrating stable pre-trained knowledge with both supervision-agnostic and supervision-conditioned evidence.
contribution: Flattens accuracy-noise curve with notable gains on OxfordPets at 75% noise (+36.6% under asymmetric, +14.4% under symmetric); transferability improvements of 2.6-15.66% when incorporated into other methods.

problem: Recent LMO-based optimizers like Muon show practical advantages but lack theoretical understanding due to overlooking layer-wise application and unrealistic smoothness assumptions.
approach: Introduces Gluon, a new LMO-based framework with refined generalized smoothness model capturing layer-wise geometry, matching practical layer-wise implementation of Muon and Scion.
contribution: Provides state-of-the-art convergence guarantees matching theoretical assumptions to practice; experiments confirm assumptions hold along optimization trajectory.
